# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (run so far)
- Strategy tried: standard diagnose→cluster→fix loop. It could not start — 10/10 val
  trajectories are sandbox-build infra failures (Docker registry i/o timeout pulling
  ubuntu:24.04), tool_calls=0 across the board. No gradient exists.
- Plateau/stall signal: this is a HARD environmental stall, not a search plateau. The
  gate re-scores on the same tasks; if the registry is still unreachable, ANY candidate
  (including a no-op) scores 0.000 and is rejected. Search cannot distinguish good edits
  from bad ones under total infra failure — the run is effectively blind.
- Lever switched to: none available. Chose a disciplined NO-OP over speculative edits,
  because with zero rollouts an edit cannot be REAL or VERIFIED and only adds regression
  risk if the network later recovers.
- What to try next iteration: FIRST confirm at least one rollout produced tool_calls>0
  before proposing anything. If the whole split still infra-errors, do not spend edits —
  the productive action is to surface the infra blocker (see FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS), not
  to churn the skill packages blind.
